The gap between PPI and CPI inflation in China continues to widen, both in absolute terms and relative to market expectations.
As captured by this CNBC headline, China's PPI inflation came in at 5.7%, its highest level in more than four years and exceeding the consensus forecast https://t.co/Iv1isuXGSs

The failure of a rapidly growing digital lender less than one week ago in Paraguay led, in quick succession, to the resignation of the central bank head (a former executive at the failed bank, Ueno) and then Paraguay's president, whose ties to the bank are the subject of probes. https://t.co/1x5H9FIH9Z

Oil-exporting economies in the Middle East have seen a sharp slowdown in economic activity due to disruptions to energy production and shipping. Higher energy prices have helped cushion the blow, but economic strains remain significant. https://t.co/5Jkk0COhsO https://t.co/MXigy3FPyc

Oil has fed more strongly into core inflation since the pandemic, according to this paper from Fed researchers.

But has inflation’s behavior changed? Or have supply shocks become more frequent or persistent?

The answer matters for how forcefully central banks should respond. https://t.co/otX3OqZkBC

In 1870: no toilets, no city plumbing, https://t.co/5PO8PLGa1G
